research.name: Central layer: RERA 2016 (association of allottees) - applies on top of the State regime

instruments.value: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (Act 16 of 2016): s.11(4)(e) association of allottees; s.11(4)(d) essential services until association takes over; s.11(4)(f) and s.17 conveyance of common areas to the association; s.19(5) allottee's right to documents/plans of common areas
instruments.note: RERA does NOT contain meeting, quorum, election or bye-law rules for the association. It only requires the promoter to enable the association to be formed. The detailed rules come from the State apartment/co-operative/society law. Text read via Indian Kanoon reproductions of the Act; the site says the original publication could not be verified.
instruments.source: https://indiankanoon.org/doc/65068227/ (whole Act, read to s.55) ; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/85425648/ (s.11)

instruments.value: s.11(4)(e): promoter must enable the formation of an association, society or co-operative society of allottees under the applicable laws; where there is no local law, the association is to be formed within three months after a majority of allottees have booked
instruments.note: Operative default period read in the Act reproduction and in two further secondary sources (a law-firm article and a Bihar RERA direction quoted in a search summary). 'Local laws' prevail, so for a State with its own rule (e.g. Maharashtra) the State period applies instead.

instruments.value: s.17(1) (proviso): absent a local law, the registered conveyance of common areas to the association must be executed within three months of the occupancy certificate; s.17(2) documents and plans handed over within thirty days of the occupancy certificate (law-firm summary)
instruments.note: s.17(1) timing read in the Act reproduction; the 30-day document handover read only in the secondary article.

The assignment pointed at s.4(2)(l)(d). That provision (written s.4(2)(l)(D)) is the 70% separate bank-account rule for allottee money; it has nothing to do with the association of allottees. No association-related content was found in s.4. Recorded so nobody relies on a wrong section reference.

Karnataka: a search summary says no specific State rule on forming the allottees' association was found; not independently verified.

recommended: RERA only says the association of allottees must be formed (s.11(4)(e), default 3 months after a majority of allottees book) and receive the common areas (s.17). Use the State pack for notice, quorum and election rules.
Until the association takes over, the promoter must maintain essential services (s.11(4)(d)) - keep proof of the handover date in the minutes.

research.name: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 (association of apartment owners + own bye-laws)

instruments.value: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act, 1972 (Karnataka Act 17 of 1973): s.3(d) association; s.3(n) 'majority' = owners holding 51% or more of the votes; s.11(1)(f) declaration states each apartment's voting percentage; s.16 bye-laws; s.24(2) decisions bind all owners
instruments.note: Read the Act text on Indian Kanoon (page says original could not be verified). Applies only to property submitted to the Act by a registered Declaration.

instruments.value: Bye-laws under s.16 are annexed to the Declaration; any change is valid only by a recorded amendment to the Declaration with a copy filed with the competent authority (Registrar of Co-operative Societies, or Secretary of the Housing Board for its buildings)
instruments.note: No schedule of model bye-laws appears in the Act text read; each association writes its own bye-laws covering the s.16(2) list.
instruments.source: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 s.16(1), s.3(i), https://indiankanoon.org/doc/100626373/

instruments.note: No Karnataka official model bye-laws for apartment owners' associations found. Karnataka Apartment Ownership Rules not read.

meetingTypes.type: annual / special general meetings of apartment owners

calledBy.value: As the bye-laws provide (s.16(2)(b) requires the bye-laws to state the method of calling owners' meetings; s.16(3)(c) allows bye-laws on annual and special general meetings)
calledBy.note: The Act itself sets no AGM date, notice period or requisition share.
calledBy.source: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 s.16(2)(b), 16(3)(c), https://indiankanoon.org/doc/100626373/

noticeDays.note: Notice period is left to each association's bye-laws; Act text has none.
noticeDays.source: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 s.16(2)(b), https://indiankanoon.org/doc/100626373/

noticeContent.note: not read / not verified: text could not be obtained

quorum.value: Majority of apartment owners unless the bye-laws state a different percentage; 'majority' = 51% or more of the votes (Declaration percentages)
quorum.note: Combination of s.16(2)(b) (default quorum is a majority) with the s.3(n) definition; the link between the two is my reading, not an express sentence.
quorum.source: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act 1972 s.16(2)(b), s.3(n), https://indiankanoon.org/doc/35613789/ ; https://indiankanoon.org/doc/100626373/

ordinary.note: Act does not fix; decisions taken by the voting percentages bind all (s.24(2)). Bye-laws decide.

special.note: Only fixed figure is the bye-law amendment percentage, which s.16(2)(k) leaves to the bye-laws.

weightageModels.value: Votes by the percentage of undivided interest stated in the Declaration
weightageModels.note: s.11(1)(f) (voting percentage in Declaration), s.6, s.24(2). Fixed percentages can be changed only with all owners' consent (s.6(2)).

proxy.note: Act has no proxy provision in the text read; one advocate Q&A says nothing either way. Bye-laws decide.

notes: RESEARCH ONLY, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Which Karnataka regime is MOST COMMON for an apartment complex (this Act, Societies Registration Act, or co-operative society) was not established by any source read; advocate answers say all three are used.
Pair with in-central-rera for the promoter's duty to enable an association.

recommended: s.16(2)(b): if the bye-laws set no other quorum percentage, the quorum is a majority of owners; 'majority' means 51% or more of the votes under the Declaration (s.3(n)). Check your registered bye-laws first - they override this default.
Votes follow the percentages written in the Declaration (s.11(1)(f)), not one-flat-one-vote, unless your Declaration says otherwise.
s.16(2)(a): at least one-third of the Board must retire every year (s.16(2)(a)).
The Act is silent on notice days, proxies and secret ballot - enter what your bye-laws say.
gaps: Act fixes no notice period, AGM date, requisition share or proxy rule - all in the society's own bye-laws (not read).
One-third-of-Board-retires-every-year staggered terms cannot be expressed as a single 'term years' setting.
Whether 'majority of owners' for quorum means 51% of votes or 51% of heads is an inference from s.3(n) - lawyer check advised.

research.name: Haryana Apartment Ownership Act 1983 + Rules 1987 model bye-laws (Exhibit B)

instruments.value: Haryana Apartment Ownership Act, 1983 (Act 10 of 1983): s.3 definitions ('majority' = 51% or more of votes; competent authority); s.16 bye-laws; s.24(2) decisions by voting percentage bind all; s.2 declaration within 90 days of completion/occupation certificate
instruments.note: Applies to property submitted to the Act by a Declaration. Read Indian Kanoon copy (original could not be verified). s.3(m) per the tool's section label; in the bye-laws it is by-law 2(f).

instruments.value: Haryana Apartment Ownership Rules, 1987, Exhibit B: 56 model bye-laws (notice, quorum, voting, Board, accounts)
instruments.note: Many figures are blank placeholders in the template (e.g. Board size, first AGM date). Whether an association must adopt them exactly was not verified. Source says original gazette could not be verified.

meetingTypes.type: annual and special general meetings of owners (model bye-laws 13-16)

calledBy.value: Special meeting: called by the President on a Board resolution, on a petition signed by a majority of owners, or on a request from the Housing Commissioner/Registrar; annual meeting date set per bye-laws (blank in template)

noticeDays.note: Notice to each owner at least 2 and not more than 7 days before the meeting, with copy to the Housing Commissioner/Registrar (by-law 16).

calledBy.value: President, or President/Secretary on written request of at least 3 Managers

noticeDays.note: Regular Board meeting: at least 3 days notice (by-law 27); special: 3 days (by-law 28); waiver by attendance (by-law 29)

noticeContent.note: not read / not verified: text could not be obtained

quorum.value: Owners: majority of owners present in person (by-law 10); Board: one-third of the total Managers (by-law 30)

adjournedQuorum.value: Adjourned owners' meeting: not less than 48 hours later; owners present in person, being not less than two, form the quorum (by-law 17). Adjourned Board meeting: proceeds without fresh notice if quorum present (by-law 30)

ordinary.value: Majority of owners casting votes in person (by-law 12); 'majority' = 51% of votes (by-law 2(f))

special.value: Business not in the notice at a special meeting: four-fifths of owners present in person (by-law 15); bye-law amendment: owners with at least 75% of total value (by-law 56)

weightageModels.value: Votes by the percentage assigned in the Declaration (by-law 9); joint owners: only the first-named person votes (by-law 6)

proxy.value: No proxy: 'Votes shall be cast in person' (by-law 11)

generalBody.value: Majority of owners casting votes in person

committeeElection.value: Board elected by ballot at the annual meeting (by-laws 14, 23)
committeeElection.note: Whether the ballot is secret is not stated in the summary read.

electronicVoting.note: not read / not verified: text could not be obtained

minutesDeadlineDays.note: Secretary keeps minutes (by-law 37); no deadline read.

recordRetentionYears.note: not read / not verified: text could not be obtained

memberInspectionRight.value: Accounts and statements open to members during office hours (by-law 48(4)); audited statement published by 31 July, copy to competent authority by 15 August (by-law 48(3)-(4))

electionRoles.value: Board of Managers elected by ballot; officers elected annually by the Board (by-law 33)
electionRoles.note: No returning officer in the model bye-laws.

termYears.note: Initial staggered terms of 3/2/1 years at the first AGM; successors serve 3 years (by-law 23). Board size left blank in template.

eligibility.note: not read / not verified: text could not be obtained

defaulterDisqualification.value: Owners more than 60 days in arrears on the last day of the year cannot vote in office elections or stand for office (by-law 8)

notes: RESEARCH ONLY, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. The model bye-laws are from the 1987 Rules text on Indian Kanoon (OCR quality, unverified). Which Haryana regime is MOST COMMON (this Act, HRRS Act 2012 societies, or co-operative societies) was not established; a search snippet says Haryana RWAs register under the 2012 societies Act (see in-hr-societies-act-2012).
Competent authority: Chief Administrator HUDA (HUDA areas), Director Urban Local Bodies / Town and Country Planning otherwise (s.3 as summarised).

recommended: Model by-law 16: notice of owners' meetings must go out at least 2 and at most 7 days before - unusually short; check your registered bye-laws.
Model by-law 11: votes are cast in person, no proxy. By-law 9: votes follow the percentage in the Declaration.
Model by-law 10: quorum is a majority of owners present in person; by-law 17: an adjourned meeting must be at least 48 hours later and any two owners present in person form its quorum.
By-law 8: owners more than 60 days in arrears at year end cannot vote in office elections or stand for office.
By-law 23: Board Managers serve 3 years; by-law 56: bye-laws are amended by owners representing at least 75% of total value.
gaps: Business outside the notice at a special meeting needs four-fifths of owners present in person (by-law 15) - no setting for this.
75% of value to amend bye-laws and 60-day arrears bar cannot be expressed.
Quorum 'majority of owners' read as 51% of votes (by-law 2(f) definition); a head-count reading is possible - lawyer check.

defaulterDisqualification.value: Defaulter of any society is ineligible to be a director (s.60(1)(c)); loses the vote as the bye-laws specify

notes: RESEARCH ONLY, NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Highest-quality read in this file (primary text). Later amendments (Acts 20 of 2014, 5 of 2020, 34 of 2021, 5 of 2022 per the PRS listing) not individually checked against these sections.

proxy_voting.reason: Goa Co-operative Societies Act s.28(1): every right to vote is exercised personally, not by proxy (only a defence-services member may vote by proxy)

recommended: s.28(1): vote in person, no proxy (only a Defence Services member may vote through another member); the chairman has a casting vote on a tie.
s.72(2): hold the AGM within nine months of the close of the co-operative year, and never more than fifteen months after the previous AGM.
s.58A / s.72(3): the board must call a general meeting within one month (s.58A) / thirty days (s.72(3)) of a requisition by one-tenth of members.

Rule 46(6): if a meeting fails for want of quorum it is adjourned to a later time the same day or to a date not earlier than 7 days, and the original agenda is then transacted whether there is a quorum or not.

s.59(2)-(3): board term five years; at most 15 directors. s.66(3): board election is by secret ballot (elections by the Registrar for societies with paid-up capital of Rs 25 lakh or more; smaller societies follow their own bye-laws and election rules, s.66(5)).
s.72(7): the chair signs the general meeting minutes within 30 days; s.72(6): minutes go to everyone invited within 45 days.
gaps: Notice days and quorum figure are set by the society's registered bye-laws (rule 46(2)) - not read.
Rule 46(6): the adjourned meeting may be on the same day (later hour) OR a date at least 7 days later; the product's 'minimum hours later' cannot express the same-day option, so left unset.
Election of directors must be by secret ballot (s.66(3)) but the product's secret-ballot option is set per event, so left for the Organizer.
Records: minute books and members' register must be kept permanently, other books 8 years (rule 47) - 'permanent' cannot be expressed.
Rule 46(3) ordinary resolutions: show of hands by majority of members present - 'show of hands' not a product setting.

recommended: Rule 28(2): unless the bye-laws say otherwise, give every member at least ten clear days notice with the agenda. Rule 29: at a special meeting only business in the agenda may be discussed.

Rule 30(1): quorum is one-third of members or 50, whichever is less, if the society has up to 500 members; one-third or 100, whichever is less, if it has more than 500. The 50 cap set here is right for up to 500 members only - change to 100 if you have more.

Rule 30(3): if no quorum within one hour the meeting is adjourned to a time the same day; the adjourned quorum is one-fifth or 30, whichever is less. A meeting called on requisition is dissolved, not adjourned.
Rule 25(2): resolutions pass by majority of members present; the chairman has a casting vote on a tie. Rule 36(2): a defaulter (after a 30-day chance to pay) cannot vote or stand.
Rule 38(3): committee term five years; rule 38(2): 5 to 21 committee members.
gaps: Quorum cap 50 vs 100 depends on member count (500) - the product has one cap value.
Adjourned quorum 'one-fifth or 30, whichever less' cannot be expressed (only a fixed minimum number of flats).
Requisition share for special meetings is in Act s.33 (not read), so no requisition percentage is set.
Rule 28/29 'unless otherwise provided in bye-laws' - bye-laws may change the notice period.
